name: Attachment

fieldTimestamps.description: Per-field HLC timestamps for scalar fields being changed

replayed.description: Set on a paused offline mutation being replayed: its field timestamps then arbitrate as intent time

createdBy.refDescription: The smallest user shape: id, name, slug and avatar. Embedded wherever a row names a user, such as `createdBy` and `updatedBy`.

updatedBy.refDescription: The smallest user shape: id, name, slug and avatar. Embedded wherever a row names a user, such as `createdBy` and `updatedBy`.

publicBucket.description: When true, the file is stored in the public bucket and served from the CDN without a presigned URL.

contentType.description: MIME type of the uploaded file (e.g. image/png).

convertedContentType.description: MIME type of the server-converted variant; null when none.

keys.description: Storage object keys per variant, keyed by variant name; only generated variants are present.

description: A file in an organization: a product entity that syncs to clients and works offline. It holds the file metadata and storage keys, not the file itself; a client fetches the file through a signed URL.

name: SsoEntry

status.description: Only `active` signs in; `pending` means the institution has not activated the app yet

description: The sign-in entry of one institution at one organization: the federation it goes through, the institution, the organization, and whether it is active. Public by the connection's id, which is the link an institution shares.

name: Connection

idpEntityIds.description: The institution's IdP entity ids, passed as login_hint

logoUrl.description: The institution's logo, for the entry page

description: A tenant's trust in an external party that asserts user identities: an institution reached through an SSO federation, whose members sign in to the tenant's organization. Its id is the public key of the tenant's SSO entry page. System admins manage connections per tenant; `pending` until the institution activated the service at the federation.

name: ChannelBase
description: The fields every channel entity shares, such as organization; a channel owns memberships and roles. Used where a response names a channel without its details, such as the channel an invitation is for.

name: ProductBase

createdBy.refDescription: The smallest user shape: id, name, slug and avatar. Embedded wherever a row names a user, such as `createdBy` and `updatedBy`.

updatedBy.refDescription: The smallest user shape: id, name, slug and avatar. Embedded wherever a row names a user, such as `createdBy` and `updatedBy`.

description: The fields every product entity shares, such as attachment: user-facing content that inherits access from its channel and syncs to clients. No endpoint returns it on its own; every product response starts with these fields.

example.name: Capitulus vesco cursim alter.
example.description: Veritas itaque basium a. Sufficio ter nostrum cilicium tersus ara. Earum ascit trans somniculosus.

name: StreamNotification

kind.description: Discriminant for the notification: product-entity sync vs membership change

action.description: Change kind; moveOut = the row left this path (reparent) and is no longer readable there

channelType.description: Channel entity type for membership events (e.g. organization, project)

path.description: Materialized id-path of the affected rows (root-first ancestor ids); moveOut carries the OLD path

seq.description: Org-sequence position (one order per organization, shared across product entity types)

channelId.description: Channel entity ID for grouping (e.g. projectId for tasks in unseen counts)

stx.refDescription: The sync envelope on every product write: a mutation ID, a source ID and per-field timestamps. Clients send it with each create and update; the server merges concurrent edits by its timestamps, and a client recognizes its own writes coming back by the source ID.

batchUntilSeq.description: Last sequence position for a batched notification: client should fetch range

count.description: Authoritative row count for batches: sequence ranges of different paths may interleave

spreadWindow.description: Server-suggested spread window (ms) for the lazy delta fetch; scales with channel audience and load, and the client clamps it between its priority tier bounds

propagation.description: Embedded-product propagation hint for cross-product cache invalidation

embeddedProduct.description: Product type whose change triggered the propagation (e.g. label)

hostProduct.description: Host product type whose cache should be patched (e.g. task)

hostColumn.description: Column on the host product that embeds the changed product (e.g. labels)

update.description: Host product IDs that need cache refresh

remove.description: Host product IDs that need the embedded reference removed

description: A live notification that a product entity or a membership changed, naming the entity, its path and sequence range rather than the row. It arrives as a `change` event on `/entities/app/stream`; the client then fetches the changed rows through the regular API.

name: ConnectedApp
description: An app the signed-in user consented to: its OAuth client, the scopes it may use and when the consent expires. Listed under Connected apps in account settings, where the user can revoke it.

name: Me

user.description: A full user account: profile, preferences such as language and newsletter, the MFA setting and activity timestamps. Returned to the user themselves and to system admins; other users see the `UserBase` fields.

isSystemAdmin.description: Whether the user holds the system admin role and the request comes from an allowed IP address.

description: The signed-in user, with whether they have system admin access on this request. A client reads it to learn who is signed in.

name: MeAuthData

connected.description: Whether the account already holds an identity through this connection

isNewDevice.description: The browser was first seen recently and is not the first one known.

description: How the signed-in user signs in: connected OAuth providers, the institutions of their organizations (connected or not), passkeys, whether TOTP is set up, and their live sessions. The account page lists it, where sessions can be ended and sign-in methods changed.

name: UploadToken

publicBucket.description: Whether the upload is stored public-read in the public bucket; the template decides.

description: Permission to upload files with one upload template, signed for the upload service, with the storage prefix the files land under. A client requests one before uploading; the template decides whether files are stored public or private.

name: InactiveMembership

createdBy.refDescription: The smallest user shape: id, name, slug and avatar. Embedded wherever a row names a user, such as `createdBy` and `updatedBy`.

description: An invitation to join a channel that is not accepted yet: the invited email, the role and who invited. It becomes a membership once accepted; the signed-in user's invitations list it with the channel it is for.

name: MembershipBase
description: A user's membership in a channel without its audit fields: the role it grants, plus the member's own archive, mute and menu order. Returned for the signed-in user's own memberships, and as `included.membership` on a channel they belong to.

name: ProtectedResourceMetadata
description: How an OAuth client gets an access token for this API or an MCP endpoint (RFC 9728): the authorization servers that issue tokens and the scopes accepted. A client finds it through the `WWW-Authenticate` header of a 401 response.

name: Organization

createdBy.refDescription: The smallest user shape: id, name, slug and avatar. Embedded wherever a row names a user, such as `createdBy` and `updatedBy`.

updatedBy.refDescription: The smallest user shape: id, name, slug and avatar. Embedded wherever a row names a user, such as `createdBy` and `updatedBy`.

membership.description: A user's membership in a channel without its audit fields: the role it grants, plus the member's own archive, mute and menu order. Returned for the signed-in user's own memberships, and as `included.membership` on a channel they belong to.

items.description: The smallest user shape: id, name, slug and avatar. Embedded wherever a row names a user, such as `createdBy` and `updatedBy`.

description: The channel entity every other channel nests under, owning memberships and roles. Tenant and organization are 1:1: an organization belongs to one tenant, and that tenant holds no other. Returned with `included` data: the signed-in user's membership, counts and member previews.

example.name: Spencer, Pouros and Bergnaum
example.welcomeText: Welcome to Spencer, Pouros and Bergnaum!

name: Request
description: A message from the public site: a contact message, a waitlist sign-up or a newsletter subscription. Anyone can send one, signed in or not; system admins list them.

example.message: Amitto sapiente antiquus temptatio verus mollitia.

name: ApiKey
description: A secret key a service account authenticates with, sent as `Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`. Only its prefix and last four characters are returned after creation; it can expire and be revoked.

name: ServiceAccount
description: An actor that is not a person, in one tenant: API keys run as it, and it holds role bindings like a member holds memberships. An organization admin creates one, for example with Create API key in organization settings.

name: Tenant

apiPointsPerHour.description: Max API points per hour per user within this tenant (0 = no tenant limit; the global safety ceiling still applies)

allowUnregisteredClients.description: Whether members may consent to OAuth clients that have no registration (AI clients using a Client ID Metadata Document)

organization.description: The organization this tenant holds, or null if none

description: The top-level isolation and billing boundary. Tenant and organization are 1:1: a tenant holds one organization, or none until that organization is created. System admins list and update tenants; a signed-in user can create one of their own.

name: User
description: A full user account: profile, preferences such as language and newsletter, the MFA setting and activity timestamps. Returned to the user themselves and to system admins; other users see the `UserBase` fields.

name: UserBase
description: The user fields shown to other users: name, slug, profile images, description and email. User lookups and member lists return it with the last-seen time added; member lists add the membership too.

name: UserMinimalBase
description: The smallest user shape: id, name, slug and avatar. Embedded wherever a row names a user, such as `createdBy` and `updatedBy`.

name: ApiError
description: The body of every error response. `type` is a stable code to branch on, `message` is readable text, and `requestId` identifies the request in the server logs.

name: BadRequestError
description: The request is malformed or fails validation (400). `type` names the problem, such as `invalid_request`.

name: ConflictError
description: The request conflicts with the current state (409), such as a link that belongs to another account (`user_mismatch`) or a create already in progress. Reload the current state before retrying.

name: ForbiddenError
description: The caller is known but may not do this (403): their role denies the action, a recent step-up is required, or the action is refused while impersonating. `type` names the reason, such as `step_up_required`.

name: NotFoundError
description: The resource does not exist, or the caller may not read it (404). Both get the same answer, so a response never confirms that an id exists.

name: StxBase

fieldTimestamps.description: Per-field HLC timestamps for scalar fields being changed

replayed.description: Set on a paused offline mutation being replayed: its field timestamps then arbitrate as intent time

description: The sync envelope on every product write: a mutation ID, a source ID and per-field timestamps. Clients send it with each create and update; the server merges concurrent edits by its timestamps, and a client recognizes its own writes coming back by the source ID.

name: TooManyRequestsError
description: A rate limit refused the request (429). The `Retry-After` header says when to try again; an operation's rate limiters show what is counted.

name: UnauthorizedError
description: The request carries no valid session, API key or access token, or it expired (401). Sign in again, or send a valid key or token.
